newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Sparks sees sharp rise in CBOT soybean prices.
newsitem.headline: Sparks sees sharp rise in CBOT soybean prices.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade soybean prices are set to rise sharply, especially in the nearer months, as tight U.S. stocks squeeze the market higher, U.S. grains consultant Willard Sparks said Tuesday.
He predicted a 1997 U.S. crop of about 2.60 billion bushels, and told Reuters in an interview that soybean prices would be forced up in a similar way to the sharp rise in maize prices last year.

"July may have to go $2 over November, $2.50 over November. That can happen if the new acreage is very big and the yields are very good. You know, November may go to $6 and July could be $9," Sparks said, "Most likely, July will be $9, $9.50, $9.75 and November will be $7, that's probably what will happen."

Asked whether he foresaw big imports of South American beans by U.S. crushers, Saprks said, "There have already been one or two cargoes But I don't think necessarily, because we've got the beans already in (the United States), we just need to quit exporting them."
But he said prices must rise to bring enough Argentine and Brazilian beans onto world markets.
